name: Agentic AI offensive frameworks (ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI, STRIX, HexStrike-AI), Sep-Nov 2026
description: Techniques observed in public reporting of operators using open-source agentic offensive frameworks. Score = number of independent evidence rows in examples/agentic-ai-attacks and the reference doc splunk-sentinel-query-builder/references/agentic-ai-attacks.md. Built against ATT&CK v20; T1574.001 (DLL) covers what earlier versions called T1574.002 DLL Side-Loading. Refreshed 2026-11-24: each report published after 2026-11-07 adds one to the score of every technique it evidences; the FBI FLASH consolidates vendor reporting, so it adds rows only for techniques not already present. Refreshed 2026-11-27 for six reports (Microsoft 2026-11-25, Wiz 2026-11-23, Unit 42 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-12, Datadog 2026-11-09, GTIG 2026-11-16) by the same rule. Unit 42 2026-11-24 found no behavioral marker tying its campaigns to a framework and ties one of them to CyberStrikeAI by infrastructure only; its rows are marked unattributed. Corrected 2026-11-28: pairs the sources did not support were removed or moved to a better-fitting technique, evidenced ones that had been left out were added, an entry that only restates a report the row already cites is not counted, tactics use the ATT&CK 20.1 names, and each comment names the Frameworks and Sources of its row in the reference table, which now carries every source earlier comments named (carried forward from those comments, not re-read against their reports; the reference says which rows). A second correction the same day names each report by its date, stops counting Microsoft 2026-11-25 on T1078.004 (it restates Microsoft 2026-10-21), credits Microsoft on all three interpreters its T1059 entry names, and adds T1578.002 for GTIG's jump-host instances.
